nodes.title: claude plugin eval cases that run the same tasks with and without the plugin and compare the outcome; each case states what is checked deterministically (commands that must and must not run, such as git push without approval or a commit with an assistant trailer; text the answer must and must not hold; an approval asked or a refusal given; a cap on tool calls), a judge only for what no check reads; each arm runs with only the plugin under test and proves it (a fresh directory outside any repository, CLAUDE.md, auto memory and user settings off, strict MCP, a pinned model, the plugin by --plugin-dir; a finished cell's transcript read for what the arm was given), a spending cap per arm, runs resumable per case, trial and arm, arms interleaved case by case; every deterministic check ships a passing and a failing reference that a self-test proves with no model call before any paid run; a cell that runs commands runs in a sandbox (no network beyond the model's API, an empty environment, writes only in the cell's directory); results name the date, CLI and model versions, cases, trials and cost, and say their limits; no git hook fires in an eval run (2.1.310: GIT_CONFIG_COUNT forces core.hooksPath=/dev/null and hook.*.enabled=false, and execution.env takes only EVAL_* keys), so Ennyn's commit gate is not compared there, only what the agent does; arms' PATH starts with the git path (test/eval/git-path.mjs) in a folder the arms can read (the plugin's); an arm cannot git init or clone a working copy, so repositories come from the scaffold; the arm's cwd lies inside the eval's own home repository; whether the without-plugin arm can read the plugin folder, and so the git path, is not measured: if not, the arms are not comparable; a host or infrastructure failure is an outcome of its own, never the plugin arm's failure, reported with a strict and a completed-only figure; each finished cell is keyed by a hash of its inputs (case text, arm, plugin commit, CLI and model versions, check code), and an unreadable result store stops the run instead of starting over A case's prompt never names the rule, gate or command it tests, so what is read is whether the agent gets there unasked; a must-not check (a push without approval, a commit with an assistant trailer) passes a cell only when every trial passes, never on a median; a case no arm passes in any trial is read as a broken case before it is read as a result. A cell is finished only on a terminal success with no permission denial and a result for every tool call; a grader that only reads whether the Skill tool ran stays out of the two-arm score; one placebo arm and one case where no change is right An eval arm's Bash reaches the macOS keychain service: it unlocks and reads any keychain file whose path it can read (2.1.310, 2.1.330, eval-keychain-exec). The login keychain is shut only by the read deny on the HOME the eval is given and its parent folder, so paid plugin-eval runs go only in a separate macOS account or a Linux VM. An eval grants Read, Glob and Grep by bare name or by `~` only, never by a path that reaches the HOME the eval is given. A bare or `~` grant keeps those tools to the arm's own home and the read roots and refuses that HOME (2.1.310, 2.1.330; eval-arm-read-tool-home, cycle 56 lab). A path grant that reaches HOME is read in full, since `--disallow-tools` and a case's `disallowed_tools` take bare tool names only, and no measured settings place reaches an arm (the eval's configuration, its HOME, the arm's cwd, the plugin). By the code, server-managed organization policy does reach an arm (2.1.330, unmeasured). The plugin's folder is a read root, so a plugin kept under the operator's HOME is readable to its arms through a bare grant.

Measured 2026-10-28: a committed settings.json with enabledPlugins, extraKnownMarketplaces, Bash(*) and a SessionStart hook echoing that text, and an .mcp.json with npx -y, passed the commit hook and doctor said nothing; init-scan lists only the hook event names (setup/scan.mjs:957-985). Also: a hook answering a tool call from a committed cache file, instruction text that copies itself into subagent prompts or tells reviewers what not to flag, a tool registering a git merge driver, a SessionStart hook calling the network, a plugin shipping its own permission policy

nodes.title: SECURITY.md gets a table of Ennyn's principals and boundaries: the user, a contributor whose commit lands in a project, a cloned repository before the user trusts it, a package registry, the model reading project text, another plugin; each boundary with the part of Ennyn that guards it (commit-msg hook, deps check, side-copy hook, init-scan's escaping, config paths). The security reviewer and the audit name the lower-trust principal and the crossed boundary for every security finding; an effect only the user can cause on their own machine (their own environment variable, a git config they wrote) is a robustness note, not a security finding; the table says what the hooks do not stop: a secret printed in a form no detector matches, a script that reads a secret file without naming it, and prompt-injected exfiltration (DNS, image URLs), for which the boundary is OS isolation and egress control
nodes.source: review of cloudflare/security-audit-skill (MIT, c1c8a8c), 2026-10-25: 'require a boundary and result': the lower-trust principal, the accepted input, the intended control, the crossed boundary, the affected resource; same-principal authority and self-impact are not cross-boundary results. Several of Ennyn's open security and gate nodes are shapes only the user's own environment produces (ENNYN_CONFIG naming a pipe, trace2 targets in the user's git config); Embrace The Red 2026-08-26 quotes Anthropic: 'The real boundary is OS isolation and network egress control.'; CVE-2025-55284 sent .env contents out through DNS from Claude Code (fixed in 1.0.4); cycle 2026-10-28 (14), hooks-project-gate review: a committed settings env ENNYN_CONFIG=/abs/file that does not parse makes the side-copy hook (stderr) and the style hook (systemMessage) quote the path and about 20 characters or the top-level key names to the user and the transcript, not to the model, a same-principal row; the side-copy hook's rule bodies are the project's own text, which Claude Code 2.1.310 loads raw as project instructions in the same request, so a body that imitates markers crosses no boundary

nodes.title: A serious finding (🔴/🟠) goes to a fresh agent that did not find it and tries to refute it, re-reading every quoted line and running the check again, before the author fixes it: a confirmed one is fixed; a refuted one is recorded as rejected with why; one whose deciding fact is out of reach is needs-validation, with that exact fact, no severity, and a graph node. Convergence counts the refuted ones, so fixes of findings that were not real are measured; the refuter never takes a lack of disproof as confirmation, and names the precondition the defect needs (Compound Engineering's ce-code-review validator; OpenAI's code reviewer chose fewer, checked findings over recall); the refuter is given the evidence again (the files, the diff, the saved source), never only the finding's wording; a fix of a misquote re-reads the source
nodes.source: review of cloudflare/security-audit-skill (MIT, c1c8a8c), 2026-10-25: 'the agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it'; three verdicts: confirmed, needs_validation (an exact unresolved fact, no severity) and rejected. Ennyn's evidence: fixes introduced more defects than first drafts missed (99 against 80 in the origin project; in Ennyn's cycles 2-10, 245 fix-introduced against 266 real escapes), and fixing a finding that was not real is pure risk; review of ScrapeGraphAI (MIT, 194055e), 2026-10-28: its retry step asks the model for the missing information without giving it the page

nodes.title: The security audit keeps a coverage ledger in the repository: one unit per group of the paths ennyn audit lists, times each attack class that applies, each planned, covered (the paths read and the checks run, named), candidate (finding ids), blocked (the exact missing fact), or deferred or out of scope with why; a zero-dependency validator checks it. The next audit starts from units never covered, deferred, blocked or whose files changed since; a final critic agent reads the ledger for unmapped entry points and parallel paths; the report claims 'audited' per unit only
nodes.source: review of cloudflare/security-audit-skill (MIT, c1c8a8c), 2026-10-25: the coverage ledger and validate-coverage-ledger.cjs are its coverage claim ('an architecture summary, agent count, or generic "auth reviewed" sentence is not coverage evidence'); runs are additive and changed source is revalidated; its README: in their test runs one run found about half of the vulnerabilities that repeated runs found in total. Ennyn's metrics log marks which cycles an audit covered, not which paths

nodes.title: finding-schema.md anchors each severity on the demonstrated result, in Ennyn's terms (for example: a gate silently lets through what it exists to refuse; a write leaves the project; a narrow shape or a condition the user sets; a wrong message or a valid input refused with a way around it), and says: a missing second layer where the first one holds is a hardening note, listed apart, never a reason for a round; no result stronger than the one observed is claimed; with no concrete damage the severity is lower than it feels
nodes.source: review of cloudflare/security-audit-skill (MIT, c1c8a8c), 2026-10-25: severity anchors with a high/medium test (does the result fully defeat an explicit control, or only weaken it?); defense-in-depth gaps are hardening notes. Ennyn's finding schema names four severities without defining them, while the cycle's rule 'a critical or high finding left after round two is still fixed' depends on them

nodes.title: Copies a commit adds get a warning from the commit-msg hook that names where the other copy is: a top-level definition (function, class, exported constant) whose name, ignoring case, `_` and `-`, another tracked source file already defines, and a block of N or more meaningful lines (whitespace collapsed; blank, comment and brace lines skipped) that another tracked source file already holds. The same check runs over the cycle's whole range at its end, since rebase and cherry-pick run no commit-msg hook and parallel tasks cannot see each other's helpers; doctor counts the copies the tree holds. A helper rewritten under another name with other text is not found, and the warning says so

nodes.title: budget --record also records what the cycle cost: tokens (input, cache write, cache read, output), agent time and, where Claude Code wrote it, dollars, summed from this project's session transcripts since the previous record, numbers only, never text; unmeasured when no transcript is there; the cycle report gives the cost per task, per review round and per finding found in review; usage is summed once per message id: Claude Code writes one transcript line per content block and repeats the message's usage on each (this repository's last 8 sessions, version field 2.1.306: summing per line gave 1.78 to 2.61 times the per-id sum, every repeated id with the same usage); a call that timed out or returned no JSON is unmeasured, never 0 USD; an estimate is never added to a measured cost; the greenfield intake and the first cycle are recorded the same way: token and time cost is among the most-reacted complaints about spec-kit, superpowers and Kiro (spec-kit #1492: 'usage limits are typically reached in under an hour of active work.'); also hours from the cycle's start to its closing, and the count of defects found after a closing in what that cycle landed: these two numbers decide whether a cut in the loop stays; it also counts cache tokens written after a gap longer than the cache lifetime, by agent kind. Cycle 18 runs with subagentPromptCacheTtl 1h and is compared with the number below Also the billable Actions time the cycle's pushes drew, per runner OS, from the run timing endpoint (it answers with gh's default scopes, measured 2026-11-25); unmeasured when unread, never 0
nodes.source: review of ponytail (an open-source agent skill, MIT), 2026-10-25: its band reads Claude Code session transcripts for cost, agent time and tokens per task, and leaves a cost empty rather than guess it (an unknown model, fast mode); Ennyn counts defects per cycle but not what a cycle or a review round costs; third-party cost scripts read 2026-10-29: a failed call recorded as a zero cost, and a missing estimate added in as 0; measured 2026-11-01 over 8 days: subagents wrote 242.8M cache tokens, 99.98% at the five-minute lifetime, 183.7M of them after a gap over five minutes (after a resume message 38%, a test run 35%, another shell command 27%); 171.0M of those gaps were under an hour. At list ratios a one-hour lifetime would save about 17% of subagent token cost; a subscription's weighting is unknown, and task-short-suite lowers the same number

nodes.title: A round-one fix stays in the lines its finding names. If a fix changes a line outside the hunks the round's findings quote, the fix report names that line (which finding needs it and why); otherwise the round is not closed. Each finding's fix size (lines added and removed, files) is recorded, so fix-introduced findings can be read against fix size. Imbue 2026-04 (SWE-bench Pro, one review-and-fix pass): given the full review, a Sonnet fixer changed 46 lines on average and 343 at most; with a summary, 19 and 160. On one task the score fell from 16/17 to 8/17. A fixer prompt that allowed skipping a finding it could not fix safely removed the worst regressions. The evidence is thin (one regressed task of 15, mean score not significantly moved): measure on Ennyn's own rounds before the gate refuses anything; the first write too: at landing the orchestrator lists the files a task changed that neither its brief nor its impact table names, and each is either justified in the report or removed. A change that works is no finding for a reviewer who asks only how it breaks

nodes.title: A fix for a review finding counts as covered only by a test that fails on the code before the fix. The cycle runs the tests the fix adds or changes against the round's base (a worktree at that commit). A fix whose tests already pass there is reported as not covered. superpowers asks for the covering test, its command and its output only in prose, before re-review; it starts as information, with verdicts such as proven, weak and inconclusive (NVIDIA-NeMo Guardrails), and blocks only once its false-alarm rate is known; a base run that errored leaves the proof unmade, never passed (spiculedata/saiku, the one blocking case found); it runs at the review round, not in the commit-msg hook, since fix: covers 49 of 134 commits and the hook runs no test; the reverted fix joins test/guards as a mutant learned from a real defect
nodes.source: research 2026-10-27: popular agent-workflow repositories and published studies; numbers are the sources' own, not measured in Ennyn

nodes.title: Survivor reasons that recur become skip rules. When several cycles give the same reason for the same kind of line (logging, clock reads, config flags, message text), a rule named in the config keeps mutate off such lines. The cycle report gives the share of mutants that were killed or led to a new test. Google (Petrović et al. 2021, arXiv 2102.11378): median mutants per change went from 820 to 77 with one mutant per line, then to 7 with skip rules; the share developers rated useful rose from about 15% to 89%
nodes.source: research 2026-10-27: popular agent-workflow repositories and published studies; numbers are the sources' own, not measured in Ennyn

nodes.title: Each impact-table row that names a risk gets at least one hand-written mutant that encodes that risk. Meta's ACH (arXiv 2501.12862) generated mutants from a stated concern and 571 tests that kill them; engineers accepted 73% of the 191 they reviewed. A survivor's 'equivalent' reason is checked first: if the tokens are identical once comments and whitespace are stripped, the mutant is invalid, not survived. No model's verdict on equivalence decides anything

nodes.title: Every hook Ennyn ships (the commit-msg hook and each Claude Code hook) declares in one place what it does when it throws: let the action through, or stop it. A test fails on a hook that declares nothing, or that does something else when made to throw (GSD Core: ON_CRASH, no default). config-failopen-scope is one case of this class

nodes.title: A new review.forbidden or mechanization rule can start as a warning. It becomes a refusal once test/verdicts and gate-stats over N cycles show no false refusal. A waiver (an entry in an except list) carries the cycle it ends at, and after that cycle doctor names it (Factory's linter rules; hookify's warn|block). Never for secrets or deps, which refuse from the start

nodes.title: A PostToolUse hook runs a fast check on the file an Edit or Write touched: node --check for JavaScript, else a configured command with {file}. It runs within a time limit and returns only the failing lines and their enclosing block. SWE-agent's ablation (arXiv 2405.15793, SWE-bench Lite): 18.0% with an edit-time lint guard, 15.0% without. Measure on the eval cases, with and without the hook: failed gate attempts (gate-stats) and wall clock

nodes.title: On a new model release, one cycle step is switched off for one cycle, starting with the step that caught the fewest defects. Anthropic dropped context resets, sprints and per-sprint QA from its own harness as models improved; Agent OS retired the phases that plan mode and todos now cover; the trial is judged by the escaped-defect count of cycle-cost, since severity labels are the author's judgement

nodes.title: A graph node or doc that quotes a source quotes a saved raw copy (curl, gh or git, with the URL, date, HTTP status and sha256 recorded), never WebFetch's output, which its tool description says 'answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model'. A local check finds each quoted span in the saved copy after whitespace and quote-mark normalization, refuses a challenge or login page as the copy, and on a later re-check reports a moved quote with its similarity score and fails when the quote is gone. a6f6d29 fixed five misquoted sources; which tool produced them was not measured; the first check passes only an exact match after that normalization, never a score: a 0.97 similarity threshold rates a 285-character quote with 'sınırlı olarak' changed to 'sınırlı olmaksızın' (limited to unlimited) at 0.984 against its source and calls it found; a quote missing from its own source is also searched in the other saved copies, so a wrong attribution is named as one. A re-check ends as current, stale, contradicted or unsupported; an unfetchable source is unsupported; a homepage or search URL is no source

nodes.title: A PostToolUse hook for every tool, only in a project with an Ennyn config, replaces secrets in a tool's output before Claude reads it (updatedToolOutput): (a) known values: read locally from the project's env files (.env, .env.*, paths security.secrets names) for keys named like PASSWORD, SECRET, TOKEN, KEY, HASH, PRIVATE or CREDENTIAL, and any run of 8 or more characters of such a value, cut at the separators tools cut at ($, :, =, quotes), is masked; (b) every issuer shape checks/secrets.mjs knows. The mask names the kind and length, never a character of the value. It connects nowhere and keeps no value on disk; whether it fails open or closed on an error is decided and tested. The origin project: a tool's warnings printed fragments of a secret-derived value into sessions on four days from 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-28; a Read deny rule on .env would not have fired (no tool named the file) and the issuer-shape scan has no shape for a hash

nodes.title: A gate for one decision answered in several places: the impact table's S1 row is answered by a command that lists every function and literal answering the same question as the changed one (same regex or string literals, same called predicates, near-duplicate bodies across modules), and a test fails when a change edits one of a known group of sibling sites and not the others, or adds a new near-duplicate of a decision with no entry in a sibling list; then delete the prose that asks reviewers to look for siblings Narrowed 2026-11-11 (decisions.md in the keep folder): keep only the command that answers the S1 row, every function and literal in the repository that answers the same question as the changed one (same string literals or regex sources, same called predicate); the near-duplicate-body heuristic and the sibling-group test are dropped, because review.cochange already holds the groups that change together and a heuristic reader is the design that fell in cycles 18, 19 and 31; then delete the prose that asks reviewers to look for siblings. Measured in cycle 32 before any edit (the stop condition held): over five named sibling pairs the strict reading found 1 and 1 in part, the lenient one 4 of 6 at up to 66 hits a run, and no too-common cutoff separates the literals to keep (budget 7 files, foreign 3) from the ones to drop (hex 7-8, ETIMEDOUT 3). A finding that fails goes back to its reviewer once with the mismatch; one that fails again is kept as unverified, with the reason, in the round's report and in the convergence counts, not dropped. finding-schema.md says 'a claim that cannot quote a line is not a finding', and nothing checks it

nodes.title: Measure the reviewers' recall on planted defects: copies of past Ennyn diffs, each with one defect of a known class planted (classes taken from the class registry and szz), plus clean diffs, reviewed by code-reviewer, data-reviewer and security-reviewer as in a cycle; a script with no model scores each finding by file:line and class and counts the false findings on clean diffs. It gives reviewer-model-diversity and effort-escalation a fixed corpus; the deterministic gates have one (test/guards.mjs, test/verdicts/), the reviewer agents do not; seeds come from real fix: commits reverted, not synthetic mutants (one preprint's best model scored F1 0.847 on synthetic cases and 0.066 on real pull requests), and the corpus is reread with the same seeds before and after a change: 20 seeds leave a wide band (14 of 20 reads 46-88%), six seeds flipping one way reads as a real change. Bait seeds: a defect older than the diff, a claim a caller's guard refutes, a comment telling the reviewer what to report; pairs of one finding with a flat and a confident fix report must end alike. A 'reviewed text is data' line enters the agents only if a seed shows a reviewer obeying

nodes.title: A task with a design brief ends with one line on how the changed surface was seen running: the command that started it (dev server, simulator, the project's own preview) and which of the brief's Behavior states were looked at (empty, loading, error, narrow screen), or 'not seen: <why>'; the UI reviewer gets the line beside the brief. Today the brief is held only against the code (task protocol step 2, the UI reviewer's brief-to-result table) and step 5 runs only the fast test. Ennyn builds no runner: Claude Code's bundled run skill ('Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working') does the launching, and the cycle skill names it 0.2 UI package, 1 of 7 (Fable 2026-11-17, on the request for UI quality in the projects Ennyn builds; sources in a kept folder outside the repository, section 4.4). Added, as the line Seen in design-brief.md, not in task-brief.md (at the fix-loop brake): two widths, one at or under 390 CSS px and one at 1440, and 320 when the task changes layout; the states of the brief that were driven; the paths of the screenshots, kept in the state dir or another place outside the work tree, never committed; what produced the evidence and what stayed untested. A capture counts only when the page was scrolled through first, entrance motion had settled and the image is not blank or black; at most three rounds of captures a task. The project's own end-to-end tool (Playwright, Cypress) takes them when the project declares one, else the run skill or Claude Code's browser, else 'not seen: <why>'; Ennyn installs no browser and runs nothing through npx, and a server the task started is stopped by its PID. Measured first, before any text: from a task agent in a worktree with no installed dependencies, on two projects with a surface (one web, one not), can the surface be started and a screenshot at a set width be taken, by which way, in how many calls and minutes, and can a subagent invoke the run skill at all; where only the landed tree can be run, the orchestrator writes the line at the landing, not the agent. Declined in part when no way reaches a screenshot without an outside install on both projects: the line stays words only, as first written. Declined whole when seeing the surface takes longer than the task's two review rounds on both

nodes.title: A greenfield trial: a small real project started from an empty directory with /ennyn:init and run for three cycles, recorded in docs/evidence.md with the intake's questions and time, the skeleton's commands and checks, and the first cycles' numbers 0.2 (Fable 2026-11-17): the trial's project has a user-visible surface (a small web application with one form and one list is enough), so the UI package (ui-seen-running, ui-brief-states, ui-reviewer, ui-check, ui-own-checks, ui-floor, ui-slop-tells) is read on a real project in the same three cycles: for each UI task the brief-to-result table's counts by kind, ui-check's candidates and how each was answered, what the project's own checks failed on, and the UI findings by class. It records what the intake's question 5 proposes for a web project's end-to-end tool, in three runs. The same run answers whether architecture and lifecycle practice reach a built project with no document written for it: counted at the end, imports that cross the boundary the first node set up, decisions found in two places, and tasks that changed one layer alone. A class that recurs becomes a mechanization node by the convergence ladder, never a prose guide. The trial also records what it ships (Fable 2026-11-23): the note's handed-to-users line; the manifest's licence after the scaffold against the note; and, with a planted value in an env file read through a public-prefixed variable (NEXT_PUBLIC_, VITE_), whether the built output holds it and what said so (the commit hook, the security reviewer's client-bundles line, nothing)

nodes.title: The cycle records what it and its agents start or create that outlives a command, in <stateDir>/resources.jsonl, never in the work tree: processes with their process group and listening ports, docker objects (label dev.ennyn.run=<id>, compose project ennyn-<id>), scratch databases, temp roots made by mkdtemp, worktrees (lock reason ennyn:<id>) and branches with their start commit. Each record holds what identifies it at removal time: a pid with its start time and cwd, an object id with its label, a realpath with device and inode, a base commit. `ennyn res` starts and records them; a PostToolUse observer adds what appeared since the session started (ports, docker objects, worktrees, branches) as observed, inferred records whose removal always asks. Nothing in Ennyn records any of this today Also VM profiles and their data disks (colima, lima): the profile name, the disk's realpath with device and inode, and whether the run created the profile or only started it (measured 2026-11-25: a deleted colima profile keeps its data disk unless the delete says --data) A footprint row (project-footprint) the user marks for removal enters as an observed record with its identity, so its removal is cleanup-command's, item by item on the user's yes; nothing in git history is ever a record
nodes.source: cleanup research 2026-10-29: Testcontainers' reaper: 'It relies on container labels to determine which resources were created by the package to determine the entities that are safe to remove.'; Claude Code worktrees: 'Claude Code writes a marker into the git metadata of every worktree it creates with git, and the sweep keeps any worktree without one'; codex#56380, a cleanup that 'did not inspect the directory contents or establish that the directory belonged exclusively to this task.'; codex#42244: 'associating processes with the thread/worktree that started them seems like the key'; a record alone is no proof: Claude Code's sweep 'trusts whatever `worktreePath` the job record carries' (#89199)

nodes.title: ennyn cleanup removes only what the record names and whose identity checks again at removal: it prints the plan first (each item with what its removal destroys: size, file count, untracked or ignored files, commits on no other ref) and a digest, and --apply <digest> runs exactly that plan, by argv, never a shell string, so no variable, glob or substitution widens a target; a mismatch marks the record orphaned and deletes nothing. Without asking: recorded processes (TERM to the group, KILL after a grace period, then the recorded ports checked free), recorded containers, the session temp root, clean worktrees, branches git branch -d accepts. Item by item on the user's yes: volumes, databases, worktrees holding untracked or ignored files, unmerged branches, observed records. Never: anything not recorded, a prune, a kill by name, home, the repository root and its parents, .git, stashes, tags, ignored files the record does not name (.env). It runs at task end and at cycle end before push-check, never in a SessionEnd hook A VM data disk goes without asking only when the record says this run created its profile, no profile of that name exists any more and lima shows no user of the disk; a stopped profile counts as existing, since lima shows its disk with no user (measured 2026-11-25). Any other VM disk is item by item on the user's yes, and one no record names is listed, never removed
nodes.source: users: 'Don't clean things up unless the user explicitly asks for it.' (codex), 'Deletion must be opt-in consent, not opt-out discovery.' (claude-code#59248); gemini-cli#23183: 'If any changes are detected (modified, staged, or untracked files) or if an error occurs during the check, the worktree must be preserved.'; Docker: 'Volumes are never removed automatically, because to do so could destroy data.'; Claude Code: 'SessionEnd hooks have a default timeout of 1.5 seconds.'; Conductor's docs: 'Descendants that move into another process group or session can survive and keep ports open'

nodes.title: A PreToolUse hook refuses a deletion whose target is built at run time or reaches too far: rm -r, find -delete, rmdir, git clean or a shell's remove on a variable or substitution ($T, ${T}, $(…), an unquoted glob after a variable) unless written ${T:?} or as a literal path; a target that resolves to /, a top-level directory, home, the repository root or one of its parents; a kill by name (pkill -f, killall); a machine-wide prune (docker system, volume, network or image prune without a label filter). The refusal names ennyn cleanup. It shares the hook and the measurement of push-spellings-hook (whether a deny holds in bypassPermissions); the report says a script the agent writes and then runs gets past it
nodes.source: four Claude Code incidents where cleanup of a temp directory deleted a home directory or a checkout: #75859 ('Because shell environment variables do not persist between separate Bash tool invocations'), #93099, #91676 ('a template-less `mktemp -d` fails and leaves the scratch-directory variable empty'), #102901 ('Unquoted and empty, `find $T -type f -delete` became `find -type f -delete`, which defaults to `.`.' and 'Permission deny rules such as `Bash(rm -rf*)` and `Bash(rm -r *)` did not apply'); Claude Code's own path check: 'The check applies to `rm` and `rmdir`, so other approved commands can delete critical paths too.'; #41357 and #52736: machine-wide docker prunes deleted other projects' volumes, images and networks; #90070: pkill -f stopped a sibling project's server; cycle 2026-11-02 (18): git -C <main> clean -fd gets past Bash(git clean *), so the hook must read git -C; the record of what a hook's deny does is test/reference/pretooluse.json (it holds in bypassPermissions, over an allow, in a subagent, on Monitor and PowerShell; a crash, a timeout and bad output run the call)

nodes.title: Tasks that run in parallel worktrees get disjoint port ranges through an environment variable the project's commands read (a base port per task, ten ports each), recorded with the task; a port held by a process the cycle did not start is never killed: the task takes another port and the report names the holder
nodes.source: Conductor: 'Conductor allocates ten ports to each workspace: CONDUCTOR_PORT through CONDUCTOR_PORT+9.'; Claude Code #90070: 'The correct unit of "my process" is **the port plus the working directory**, never the process name.'; claude-code#34385 asks for port allocation across sessions; codex#25772: a Next.js server left holding port 3000

nodes.title: The commit-msg hook refuses a commit that adds a scratch file outside test and fixture paths, through a config rule with an except list as review.forbidden has: *.bak, *.orig, *.swp, *.swo, *~; a report at the root named in upper snake case ending _SUMMARY, _ANALYSIS, _COMPLETE, _COMPLETION, _FIX or _FIXES .md; a root script starting debug_, tmp_, temp_ or scratch_. The refusal says to delete the file or move what it holds into the handoff or the graph. Writing such files stays free; only committing them is refused. Broad names (_v2, _new, _old, _copy, _simple, check_) are never matched
nodes.source: measured 2026-10-29: the precise names matched one file (a fixture under tests/) in 99,130 files of 8 mature repositories ('blobs in 8 trees 99130') and matched in both agent-heavy repositories sampled; GitHub code search for IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md: 100608 files; Anthropic's prompting guide: 'Claude’s latest models might sometimes create new files for testing and iteration purposes, particularly when working with code.'; Cursor forum 136214: 'fix_v1.ts through fix_v20.ts'; counter-evidence claude-code#44657, a block on writing such files: 'It breaks established workflows where subagents are explicitly instructed to write results to files.'

nodes.title: The commit-msg hook warns, never refuses: a code file the commit adds that no tracked file references by path, basename or stem (tests, migrations, workflows, config files read by name and entry points excluded); a dependency the commit adds to a manifest that no file names (said as unmeasured where the import name cannot be derived from the package name); two or more added comment lines that compile as code (for JavaScript a node:vm Script compiled, never run); a test_*.py at the root when the project has a test folder. Measured on 7 human-maintained repositories: the unreferenced-file check flagged no code file in 1,913 commits, the dependency check flagged 4 of 66 additions and nearly all were false positives, hence warnings
nodes.source: probe totals 2026-10-29: 'commits=1913', 'code_unreferenced_at_add=0', 'deps_added=66 deps_no_name_match=4', 'commented_blocks=2'; agent-heavy sample: 'code_unreferenced_at_add=2' (both wired in by a later commit); arXiv 2511.04427 on Cursor adoption: 'Static analysis warnings increase by 30% and code complexity increases by 41% post-adoption'; arXiv 2512.20334: defective commented-out code in the context raises defective output 'up to 58.17 percent'

nodes.title: init proposes the ecosystem's leftover tool when the project has none and records its command, never installing it and never through npx: knip for JavaScript and TypeScript (not depcheck, unimported or ts-prune), deptry and vulture for Python, go mod tidy -diff with staticcheck and deadcode for Go, cargo-machete for Rust. These tools run project code (knip loads config files), so the command gets the trust the test command has. The cycle's closing and the legacy audit run it
nodes.source: depcheck's README: 'We strongly recommend switching to knip'; unimported: 'This project is no longer maintained'; knip: 'Knip loads and executes config files'; deptry: 'Installing _deptry_ globally will not work'; cargo-machete: 'text search isn’t syntaxic analysis'; cycle 2026-11-02 (18): lean-audit shipped skills/cycle/lean-audit.md; running the tool on the audited feature's files waits for this node, and that file names the line; cycle 2026-11-02 (19), cycle-leftover-report: its two heuristic parts (files the cycle added that nothing names, dependencies nothing names) were cut after review: on a corpus of ordinary shapes 19 of 28 used files were listed and 9 of 15 real leftovers missed (imports without extension, files read by convention or by a computed name, word boundaries, common-word package names), and this repository's history held no true leftover in 19 cycle windows. A language-aware tool models what that reader could not; until init records one, the closing says that part unmeasured

nodes.title: budget --record also records the disk use of the cycle's worktrees, its temp roots and Ennyn's state folder, and the cycle report says the growth; Ennyn's own state and logs stay within a size the config names. No agent tool measures this, and users report tool folders of tens to hundreds of gigabytes. Acceptance run 2026-11-15: the state folder under the git dir reached about 1.2 GB after two cycles of a small library (review trees, mutation copies with node_modules), nothing reported it The record also holds project-footprint's totals by kind, numbers only, so growth between closings is read from the metrics log and the audit's comparison starts from the last record
nodes.source: claude-code#24207: 'The `~/.claude` directory grows unbounded, there is no monitoring, no cleanup mechanism, and no user warnings.'; Codex: 'Worktrees can take up a lot of disk space. Each one has its own set of repository files, dependencies, build caches, etc.'; codex#39421: 559 GB of staging folders; Ennyn's own test-temp-cleanup (done): the suite had left about 160 GB and a full disk by cycle 9

nodes.title: A task that needs a database uses a scratch one: on a server the resource record names (a container with Ennyn's label, a temporary server, a local socket), with a name that starts with ennyn_, created from a template; a drop, reset, force-reset or fresh migration runs only against such a database. The agent never points a scratch, test or shadow database at a URL read from an env file, and init asks whether the project's local env files can reach production data, recording the answer, never the URL
nodes.source: Replit, July 2025, after its agent deleted a production database: 'automatic separation between development and production databases'; claude-code#36183: 'The DATABASE_URL in .env points directly to the production database.'; #80868: 'Prisma resets the shadow database (drops all objects) before replaying migrations.'; Postgres: 'DROP DATABASE cannot be undone. Use it with care!'

nodes.title: Each test, mutation or server command the cycle runs is wrapped in a snapshot of what a command can leave behind, taken before and after, and the difference is reported as left behind by that command (what resource-ledger records is explained, once it exists): untracked and ignored files in the work tree (git status --ignored), new entries in the temp folder, docker containers, volumes, networks and images, listening ports and processes whose cwd is in the repository or its worktrees, git worktrees, branches and stashes, global installs (npm -g, pip outside a virtualenv, brew, cargo install, go install, pipx), changes to the user's config files (~/.gitconfig, ~/.npmrc, shell profiles), and databases on the local servers the project declares, through a listing command init records, never a URL. It catches what no list names; the snapshot only reads, and removing stays with cleanup-command Also VMs and containers: what a cycle starts (colima profile, docker container, dev server) is stopped by what started it, and the closing lists those running that were not at the start (cycle 33 left colima ennyn-ci running 13 h, 1.6 GB). The closing report says memory, swap, load and free disk at the start and the end The snapshot also reads VM data disks (limactl disk list beside colima list), and the closing lists each disk whose profile is gone, with its size on disk

nodes.title: init, and the legacy audit when it audits the test setup, runs the project's fast test command once inside run-leftover-diff with TMPDIR pointed at a temp root the cycle owns, and reports what the suite leaves behind: a test database a crashed or --keepdb run kept, SQLite files, containers when the reaper is off, temp folders, worker processes, coverage output that is not ignored. A suite that leaves something becomes a graph node, as Ennyn's own did: test/hermetic.mjs removes each test file's temp root at exit since the suite filled a disk 2026-11-14: Ennyn's own suite and agents' labs left 3356 temp folders in five days on the Mac; the temp churn is the likely driver of fseventsd's and the kernel's memory (measure first)

A Linux run costs about an hour, so the cheap layer should catch the first

nodes.title: 'Closed' is proven and watched: a class reaches closed-gate only when its past defects put back (reverted fixes, verdict cells that carry a `class`) and at least one variant turn the gate red; each closing recounts the class and writes the exposure (lines changed in what the gate guards), a recurrence reopens the class and moves its action up a level, and zero recurrence with no exposure is no success. Run back over the 12 gates born from convergence reports. test/guards.mjs tests a gate against mutants of its own check, not against the defect class
nodes.source: 2026-10-31 research on closing escaped classes: of those 12 gates none is shown to stop its class: 7 partial, 1 stopped nothing, 4 with almost no exposure (judgement); the class moves to the next surface under a new name. The second project's gate did this: red on 6, 42 and 14 cases. No product or study found publishes whether a class stopped, and the three-part definition of closed is inference

nodes.title: The commit hook records every refusal and pass through gate-record, so `ennyn gate-stats` has data, and each gate gets a false-alarm reading (an `except` entry as 'not useful', a code change as 'please fix'); rule-warn-then-block, test-weakening-warn and gate-loosening-guard read it
nodes.source: 2026-10-31 research on closing escaped classes: gate-stats reads no attempts because the hook never calls gate-record, so a refusal leaves no record; Google's Tricorder keeps a check only under a measured false-positive bar

nodes.source: 2026-10-31 research on closing escaped classes: an unmeasured state read as a result is about 9% of coded findings (±25%) and came back at logic level past the fault matrix in cycles 8 to 11 and 15; fault-matrix-writes, rework-says-unread and config-failopen-scope are partial. Derived from the class, not tried

nodes.title: code-reviewer.md names two more breakers: a workaround that needs a paragraph-long comment to justify it, and a stub or placeholder standing where the task asked for behaviour. Run with reviewer-seeded-recall, so the line stays only if it finds something. A third: a test whose expected value is computed the way the code computes it

nodes.title: Each mutant runs only the test files that load its file, read from the impact-scoped-tests map; a full list runs before a release, because a change in another file can weaken a test. No random sampling: the aim is surviving mutants, not a score
nodes.source: measured, cycle 16: mutation gave 37 findings, 0 high, 3 medium, for 4.74 agent-hours of waiting; 31 of the 37 closed with a test, which is its product; T4 narrowed by hand to one test file and finished its first pass in 4.1 + 9.1 minutes, T2b's first run took 43.8 alone (different mutants and load, so direction only). Stryker and cargo-mutants also ask for a periodic full run

nodes.title: A brief names the one measurement its task's claim rests on; the author runs it before writing the rest, and when it does not hold, writing stops and the task goes back to the orchestrator. No separate plan reviewer. Enforced by the brief's table, since a limit that lives only in prose gets lost. A design decision a brief states is a claim to measure as well: refuted, the agent stops and says so
nodes.source: measured, cycle 16: the two longest items were T2's rewrite (191 minutes) and first design (149); T2's own lab showed 0 of 9 recorded compactions would be held as soon as the writing ended, and the design changed only after review. superpowers removed its plan reviewer after 5 trials over 5 versions showed the same quality at double the time, and lost a five-round limit to a compaction, running 18 rounds (its release notes, self-reported); cycle 2026-11-01 (17), carried by hand in every brief: T1's measure took 2 minutes and held; T2's found the cause was no load at all, in about an hour, before a fix was written; T5 stopped at a critical (an unstaged config edit) and it became T4's scope; T5b stopped on a third test on git 2.39.5; T3b's stop table made the scope rule. None of them lost a design to a late review; cycle 2026-11-02 (18), by hand in every brief: T3's stop found a real wrong verdict in 20 minutes, T2's found a size limit and the deny held, T2b's and T2c's held the redesigns to numbers; a design the orchestrator wrote in a brief was refuted three times, each by measurement: 'Bash(gh api * -X POST *)', the undo rule, sole-plain-only; cycle 2026-11-02 (19), brief-rules-in-skill's gap table (G1, G2): both did work in cycles 17-18 and are absent from the shipped text; in cycle 19 every brief carried a stop condition by hand, and three fired before any code (T1 a node wider than its list, T2 the hook's folder, T3 a predicate that lost data)

nodes.title: A pure function of the diff picks review depth: size and a path list, where a small config change is never trivial and a floor can only move depth up. Round two reads the diff of the fixes only. Round one stays, and so does round two after a fix that changes behaviour. review.impactRequiredGlobs gains skills/**, agents/** and hooks/**
nodes.source: measured, cycle 16: round two gave 34 findings, 23 born of a round one fix; T3a's took 11 minutes and found 3 high, T1's took 52. T1 looked like docs and tests, changed skills/cycle/ and gave 9 medium in round two; those paths are outside the glob list. Saves little here, since most of Ennyn is gates, hooks or rule text. Cloudflare picks tiers by diff size and a path list; gstack uses a pure function, Compound Engineering a floor that only moves up; a small config change escaped Meta's risk score (CORA, ESEM 2026). Agents skipped the design in 6 of 6 runs when superpowers let the model decide size

nodes.title: ennyn run --cycles N (or --each task) from the terminal: each cycle or task is one claude -p with the cycle skill, a new process and so a new context. --cycles is required, there is no open-ended loop; a budget cap goes to --max-budget-usd. It runs doctor first and stops at the first red: non-zero exit, a stopped task, a gate that needs the user, the plan's limit, the budget; it prints why and what is next, and keeps a log in the state dir. It spawns only the claude on PATH. It decides from the journal, never from the model's words, and a run with no new commit and no node change ends the loop. With compact it resumes by session id, never --continue. Pushes follow push.mode. A -p run cannot ask, so it needs a mode that does not prompt (the no-bypass mode or the user's own bypass), and it says so when it has neither. Measure first (the first two from cycle 50, Fable 2026-11-21): one write of words/<id>.txt under .git/ in claude -p (in an interactive bypass session, 2.1.327, the Write tool and a Bash redirect did not prompt): if it prompts, the write moves into an ennyn command, which reopens the declined id check; permissions.denyInsteadOfPrompting passed to each child with --settings (its text in the 2.1.327 to 2.1.329 binaries: a call that would prompt is denied at once, subagents included): whether an ask rule then denies rather than waits, unmeasured; a task with subagents completes in -p, an ask rule refuses rather than hangs, hooks and the plugin load without --bare, and what breaks if --bare becomes the default for -p. If this threatens the release date it moves to the next version, ahead of everything else there; the 5-hour usage window does not end the run. The run reads claude -p's stream-json events, never the model's words: a rate_limit_event whose status is rejected and whose resetsAt is at most 5 hours away makes it wait until that time plus a minute and go on from the journal, and the cycle it cut does not count against --cycles; a later resetsAt (a weekly window), no resetsAt, or errorCode credits_required stops it as before, saying when the window resets. At a seam, when the last event said allowed_warning with a resetsAt within 5 hours, it starts no new cycle before that time. No threshold key: the warning is the server's. rateLimitType and unifiedWindows are in 2.1.310's schema but not in the docs, so they are not read. Measure first: what -p does when it is refused (exit status, whether the event comes before the result), at what use the server sends allowed_warning, and that a cycle cut mid-task resumes from the journal. A stopped task still ends the run: the next cycle could take the same node again, or build on work the user has not seen. It reports a silent stall (no stream event and no journal line for longer than the longest past step) and stops nothing by itself. Amended 2026-11-17 (Fable, after the audit runs of cycles 36-40, prototype runner scripts kept outside the repository): the first run of 0.2, from 2026-11-29. The child gets an allowlisted environment: a parent session's identity variables (session id, messaging socket, child-session mark) and GIT_* are dropped, auth and provider variables kept (measure first: hygiene, not a proven fix). --each <node> <node>... takes a list fixed at start; a second ennyn run queues behind the first on a lock, no open-ended queue. The runner is detached with its PID recorded; nothing between items reads stdin or waits for a session, and no step runs through a host that can show a permission prompt (in the audit runs an interactive session's git push waited on a git push ask rule until it was answered). A wait is not red: a loosening key, a user gate or an asked push under ask is recorded as a wait, that node and its dependants are skipped and the run goes on when the tree is clean and the closing complete; red still stops it. A result event with the journal still open is red. The runner holds the wake lock for each child's lifetime and the brief's own wake step is skipped under it. The runner never pushes; only the closing does, under push.mode

Option B, remove the need: the intake shrinks to the one question the first commit cannot do without, and the rest stays the user's to write. Leftover defects it carries, not fixed one by one: a rerun repeats the intake; the closing's handoff rewrite drops the Product: line; lint and typecheck choices kept only as prose; no guard pins the intake rules; line 18 'in one message' beside the two-message exception; what a question tool returns after askUserQuestionTimeout is unmeasured (the stand-in model on 127.0.0.1 can measure it). Under either option ui-own-checks reads the tool from what the project declares, so it needs no intake answer. Under option A the end-to-end answer is one of the kept answers, and its proposal for a browser surface is the stack's usual browser runner (Playwright at the time of writing), its name and version from the registry at the time of choice (greenfield-stack-versions, preinstall-name-check), its browser download a step the user starts, never through npx and never by Ennyn. nodes.title: The session's model decides and writes no code: a trial of two cycles, then the rule. Today the brief's Model row puts code, gates and security on the session's model (model-per-role), so the strongest model both decides and writes, through a task agent. Trial: in the first two cycles after 0.1.0 in this repository every author runs on the model one step below the session's, set on the Agent call by the brief's Model row (a config key names it once code lands, never a model's name in the shipped text), while the orchestrator (plan, briefs, verdicts, landing) and the reviewers stay on the session's. The rule ships as the default when, over the two cycles, fix-introduced and escaped findings per task are no higher than the mean of the five cycles before and no more tasks stop than in those five together; otherwise authors go back to the session's model and the numbers go to docs/evidence.md. What holds it: during the trial the closing lists every author that ran on the session's model (ennyn agents), and a PreToolUse hook that refuses an edit of a code file from the main thread while a cycle is open comes only after a measurement shows the hook input tells a subagent's call from the main thread's on the installed version. It applies to Ennyn's own cycles first and to the projects that run them once it is the default; effort-escalation lowers the effort, this lowers the model An author never runs on Fable, whatever the session is (the user, 2026-11-12: a request): when one step below the session would be Fable, the author runs on the next model that is not. Leftover findings of the bullet: stop when the run stops named only there, no stopping path points to it (c43-t1-correctness-r1-02, c43-t1-security-r1-06); the stop passes the kill hook only when the folder path is unquoted or quoted whole, and the placeholder pasted as is is refused (c43-t1-correctness-r1-04, c43-t1-security-r1-05); one record for the clone, so two live sessions on one clone overwrite it (c43-t1-security-r1-01); a start under a nested shell ties the wake to the call's own shell and nothing checks the hold took (c43-t1-security-r1-04). Measured 2026-11-17 in a terminal runner: $PPID of a Bash call is the claude process; caffeinate <utility> holds from a child, so a walk up $PPID finds no caffeinate and pmset is the reading. nodes.title: 0.2 UI package, 3 of 7: the plugin ships agents/ui-reviewer.md, the reviewer skills/cycle/design-brief.md names (lines 5 and 19) and agents/ never held: it ships code-reviewer, data-reviewer, security-reviewer, scout and summarizer. Step 7 of the cycle skill adds it to Ennyn's three, or to review.agents, only for a task with a design brief; no config key. model: inherit, tools Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, no Write or Edit, the other reviewers' rule on stopping processes. Its contract, in Ennyn's words. It looks before it reads: the screenshots first, described in its own words, then the brief, then the code, and the author's report last, because an author's account of what was done is no evidence. Its report opens with the brief-to-result table, one row per brief line and per Behavior state: met (file:line or screenshot), adapted (the brief line that allows it), missing, contradicts, unrequested, or not seen; these are the finding schema's requirement kinds. 'Not seen' is counted and never reported as met: a width or a state with no capture was not seen, and a check that did not run is never a pass. A finding is a departure from the brief, a ui-check candidate it confirms, or a row of ui-floor.md; a preference with none of those behind it is counted in one line and not listed. One tell proves little: tells count where they cluster or repeat. After the table, ten questions in its own words (is status shown, the users' words, a way back, the same thing meaning the same, mistakes prevented, nothing to remember, faster paths for the frequent, every element serving the task, errors that say what to do, help in context), credited to the ten usability heuristics by one reference line, none of their text. It changes nothing and proposes no redesign of a screen the brief is met on. A guard in test/plugin.test.mjs fails when a file under skills/ names a reviewer no file in agents/ supplies: the class of this defect. Measured first, before the agent is written in full: one small page built to a brief with at least six planted departures, one of each kind (a state missing, no narrow layout, a keyboard trap, a Components name absent from the code, a Direction the result does not show, an undeclared deviation from the design file), reviewed three times each by the code-reviewer given the brief and by the draft UI reviewer, with and without the screenshots, and once reading code first; counted: planted departures found, other findings that hold, findings that do not hold. Declined when the code-reviewer given the brief finds as many planted departures (within one) and the screenshots add none: then step 7 hands the brief to the code-reviewer in one clause, design-brief.md's two mentions of a UI reviewer are reworded, and no agent ships. nodes.title: 0.2 UI package, 4 of 7: ennyn ui-check, a command with no dependency and no browser that prints candidates on the files it is given, a task's changed files by default: file:line, a rule id, the line. Bug-class rules, accessibility and correctness that 3 to 12 of the 16 sources read state and none disputes: a focus outline removed with no focus-visible replacement in the file; an animation or transition in the project and prefers-reduced-motion nowhere in it; img without alt; an input with a placeholder and no label or aria-label; a button that holds only an icon and no name; a div or span with a click handler and no role and tabindex; zoom locked (user-scalable=no, maximum-scale=1); paste blocked; a positive tabindex; generic error strings ('Something went wrong', 'An error occurred', 'Invalid input'); generic link and button text ('Click here', a lone 'Submit' or 'OK'); placeholder residue (lorem ipsum, [Company Name]). Tell-class rules: the 'by command' rows of ui-slop-tells. And ui-check --contrast <text> <ground>: the WCAG 2.2 ratio by the normative formula, against 4.5, 3 for large text and 3 for non-text, never rounded up, pinned by #767676 on white passing at 4.54 and #777777 failing at 4.48, so no model works out a ratio from memory. It is no gate: exit 0 with candidates, never in the commit hook. The report's Checks line says 'ui-check: N candidates, each answered' or 'not run', and not run is never a pass; the UI reviewer answers every candidate as a finding, 'no defect: why' or 'chosen: <brief line>'. Rules are line patterns in one table with id, class, source and date, each with an accept and a reject line in a corpus under test/; no markup is parsed, nesting is not followed, and its output says so. What keeps it out of the fix loop: a pattern that needs an exemption list to pass its corpus is not patched, it leaves the command and becomes a reviewer-only row; at most 30 patterns. The patterns are Ennyn's own, written from each rule's description: no regex, word list or code is copied from impeccable, taste-skill, ui-ux-pro-max or the Vercel list, and none of those is installed or run. A token or DESIGN.md file is not read (a YAML reader with no dependency is the reader trap this project knows); --contrast takes the pairs as arguments. Measured first, before any code: each candidate pattern run by plain git grep over ui-reviewer's trial surfaces and one existing web project at hand; for each pattern: hits, hits a reader confirms, false alarms. A pattern is kept when a reader confirms at least two thirds of its hits and it hit at least once. Declined whole when fewer than eight patterns are kept: then --contrast alone ships and the kept patterns go to ui-floor.md as reviewer rows

nodes.title: ennyn footprint reads what the project already holds on disk and how it got there, and only reports: no deletion, no git gc or prune, no history rewrite, no project code run. Nothing reads this today: every disk node measures what a cycle adds from now on. Git and Node only, by argv with a time limit. (a) Git: count-objects (pack, loose, garbage), the ten largest blobs any ref reaches with path, the date of the commit that added each and whether HEAD still holds it, the LFS store's size under the git dir with the paths .gitattributes sends there (no git lfs call), and tracked files an ignore rule matches (output that was committed). A shallow or partial clone is said and nothing is fetched. (b) Work tree: each top-level ignored or untracked directory and large file (git ls-files --others, with and without --ignored, --directory) with allocated bytes, entry count, newest change date and a kind by name (dependencies, build output, cache, coverage, logs, database files, virtual environments, temp). (c) Worktrees: each linked worktree's size, its dependency folders, whether git calls it prunable and whether its branch is merged; Ennyn's own state folder. The walk uses lstat only, follows no link, stays inside the root and on its device, counts a hard link once and counts allocated blocks, not length (measured 2026-11-25: a sparse VM disk of 100 GiB nominal size held 1.6 GB; where the platform gives no block count, the length, said); past an entry cap or the time limit the rest is unmeasured, never none. Output is names and sizes through the report's escaping, never a file's content. Where it runs: init-scan --json carries it as footprint and init's report gets one line (the total and the three largest); the legacy audit runs it once and lists under the lean group each row that is new or grew since the last record. A row whose cause the project can fix (committed output, a large blob added lately, dependency copies per worktree) is proposed as a node on the user's yes; plain stock is a line. Tests build their repositories in temporary folders
nodes.source: the user, 2026-11-25: a request

nodes.title: ennyn footprint also lists what the project left outside its folder, report only. An object is the project's when a label holds the project's root path or a tracked file of the project names it; anything else is not listed and not counted. (a) Docker: containers, networks and volumes by the compose labels (working directory under the root; a volume by the compose project name, said as inferred since another folder of the same name matches too), images and VM profiles only by a name a tracked compose file or script gives; each with size and creation date, read from listings, never from inspect's environment. (b) Processes whose working directory is inside the root or a worktree, with their listening ports: process name, pid and age, never arguments or environment. (c) Scheduled jobs and background services that name the root (the user's crontab, launchd agents, systemd user units): the count and where each lives, never the line. A tool that is absent, a daemon or VM that is not running (none is ever started to measure) or a listing past its time limit is unmeasured, never none; Windows is unmeasured until read there. Commands run by argv; tests feed recorded listings through stand-in commands on a temporary PATH, no docker needed. The listing code is the one run-leftover-diff's snapshot uses: whichever lands first writes it. Measure first on three real projects how much (c) finds; if nothing, it leaves the node

nodes.title: push-check says what the push will start and what that draws on, before the push; nothing reads this today. (a) No network: from the tracked workflow files, the workflows whose triggers match the refs being pushed (branch, tag and path filters read; a job's if is not evaluated and counts as may run) and each job's runner. With the repository's visibility (through gh when it is on PATH; else unmeasured) each job is metered or not: every GitHub-hosted job of a private repository, only a larger runner in a public one, no self-hosted job. No metered job: one line, and nothing else is read. (b) Else the readings, numbers only: the repository's billable time this billing cycle per runner OS and the last runs' billable time as the estimate for this push (the workflow and run timing endpoints), said as a lower bound of the account's; the account's own usage, with Actions storage, Packages and Git LFS, when the token can read the billing usage endpoint. Measured 2026-11-25, gh 2.92.0 with its default scopes: the timing and cache usage endpoints answer, every user billing endpoint answers 404 and gh names the user scope. Ennyn never widens a token: it says the command and reports that reading unmeasured. (c) The config names the month's limit in minutes and the share to warn at; no plan's numbers are held in code. Past the share: a warning. Metered jobs with a reading at or past the limit, or a limit set and no reading: exit 3, the push is asked and the cycle does not make it by itself. No limit set: lines only. Unreadable is unmeasured, never ok and never 0. It never dispatches, reruns or cancels a workflow to measure, and prints no token and no account name. Also one line when gh api rate_limit, free to read, shows under a tenth left. init-scan lists the same workflow-by-runner table, and init proposes the limit only for a private repository with a push or pull request workflow. The closing report carries push-check's line. Tests feed recorded answers through a stand-in gh on a temporary PATH, no network
